Senses.Explanation: Make it oneself and receive it oneself joins an act to the consequence borne by the same person. Chan masters use it both as a direct verdict returned to someone’s complaint and as a first-person acknowledgment of a burden they have taken on. Juelang uses it in a question about personal conduct and consequence; Baichi says it after no one offers rescue; Zhe’an applies it to his own burden in a self-portrait; and Huangbo applies it to views his listeners themselves produce and carry.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: The ordinary responsibility formula becomes a compact encounter verdict and a master’s self-description, without requiring an imported theory of posthumous reward.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The phrase assigns act and receipt to one person in these contexts; it does not by itself define every causal relation in the corpus.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: The repeated 自 explicitly binds cause and receipt to one agent in one responsibility formula.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: The probes retain self-making, self-receiving, consequence, and bringing something on oneself.

ModifierControls.Finding: The two 自 graphs require the maker and receiver to be the same person.
